standard_prerequisites: A type with an element and paths, and the identity type of that type.
Transport along a path in a type family, applied to families of identifications.
Path composition, path inverse, and the unit laws for composition.
Path induction with its conversion rule.
core_obligations: Prove the three transport computations: transport in the family taking x to the identification of the fixed element with x equals post-composition with the path; transport in the family taking x to the identification of x with the fixed element equals pre-composition with the inverse of the path; transport in the family taking x to the loop space at x equals pre-composition with the inverse of the path followed by post-composition with the path.
proof_roadmap: Apply path induction to the path, reducing to the reflexivity case.
In the reflexivity case each claimed composite reduces to the input path by the unit laws for composition (author lemma 2.1.4).
difficulty_reason: Three symmetric one-step computations, each an induction closed by the unit laws; the care point is keeping the three family shapes and their composite directions apart.
